summary.intent: Conduct a security review of the feat/store-ipns-crypto-data-in-db branch, implement identified fixes, and get the PR merged through CI.
summary.outcome: Security review completed with report written, all HIGH/MEDIUM findings fixed and committed, PR #448 created, and CI failures resolved (ESM/CJS bundling conflict, test fixture mismatch, missing dependency build step in CI workflow).

repo: @cipherbox/crypto uses @libp2p/crypto, @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, and multiformats which are all ESM-only packages — they cannot be require()'d in CJS environments like NestJS without bundling
The NestJS API runs as CommonJS; any workspace package consumed by it must either ship a self-contained CJS bundle or use dynamic import()
IPNS names are cryptographically derived from Ed25519 public keys via deriveIpnsName() from @cipherbox/crypto — the pubKey-to-ipnsName binding was not being verified on resolve
The web app (apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts) was not sending publicKey on publish, making the new server-side binding check dead code for web-published records
The web app used spread operator for base64 encoding (String.fromCharCode(...bytes)) which causes call-stack overflow on large IPNS records
The CI 'Verify API Spec' job ran pnpm api:generate without first building @cipherbox/crypto, causing build failures after the new dependency was added

code.finding: Must use split CJS/ESM build configs: CJS uses noExternal: [/.*/] to bundle all deps inline (for NestJS/Jest), ESM keeps deps external (for Vite/Rollup browser builds). A single config with noExternal breaks the desktop Vite build due to Buffer not being available in browser.

After verifying Ed25519 signature, must also derive IPNS name from returned pubKey and compare to requested ipnsName — otherwise a compromised server can substitute its own keypair and pass signature verification.
Must use loop-based base64 encoding (not spread operator) and must derive + send publicKey on publish. Both were missing before this session.

Test fixtures must use IPNS names that actually derive from the test public keys — dummy ipnsName values like 'k51qzi5uqu5dg12345abcdef67890' will fail once server-side pubKey-to-ipnsName binding validation is enforced.

The 'Verify API Spec' job needs an explicit 'pnpm build --filter @cipherbox/crypto' step before building the API, since the API now depends on @cipherbox/crypto which is not built by default in that job.

workflow: When adding an ESM-only package as a dependency to a CJS-consuming workspace package, always verify the full build works (API start + desktop Vite build) before pushing to CI
Verify the API actually starts locally (not just compiles) before pushing — runtime require() failures don't appear at compile time
Security review findings should be cross-checked: the same vulnerability (missing pubKey binding) existed in both sdk-core and the web app service layer
When updating server-side validation that checks against persisted data, update test fixtures to use real derived values rather than arbitrary dummy strings

friction: Three separate CI failures required three fix commits: (1) @libp2p/crypto ESM-only, (2) @noble/ed25519 also ESM-only requiring noExternal: [/.*/], (3) desktop Vite build broken by noExternal on ESM output — each was only discoverable by running CI
1Password SSH agent caused intermittent commit signing failures requiring retry
The 'verify api spec' CI job failure was only discoverable after pushing — no local equivalent of that job exists to run beforehand
Security review was interrupted mid-session by usage limits, requiring the report compilation to be restarted
open_items: Signature verification downgrade attack (Finding #4): callers of resolveIpnsRecord don't enforce signatureVerified===true — server can omit signature fields and bypass verification entirely. Deferred as a design decision.
Inconsistent key zeroization (Finding #5): private key bytes are not cleared from memory after use in crypto functions. Deferred as a convention issue rather than concrete vulnerability.
The security review report at .planning/security/REVIEW-20260402-172126.md marks these as deferred with notes, but they remain unaddressed technical debt.
